extracted.intended_audience: scientists, naturalists, travelers, and authors of popular scientific works; educated general readers interested in physical history of the universe
extracted.subtask_short: writing physical history of the universe
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing a physical history / popular-science exposition of the universe: how to combine patient observation, measurement, and interdisciplinary knowledge into general, accessible, empirically grounded accounts without unnecessary technical scaffolding or speculative abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of general views over mere accumulation of details
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere accumulation of unconnected observations of details, devoid of generalization of ideas, is inadequate; general considerations are often more attractive and afford superior advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suppress unnecessary detail so that 'the great masses are better seen'; emphasize the general results ('beacon lights of science') rather than the long series of means. Avoid producing works that are inaccessible through excessive listing of minutiae (critique of German scientific works).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and patient measurement in observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient, repeated measurements and careful counting (e.g., heliometer measurements, meridian altitudes, counting stamens, microscopic observation) are essential to the sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate instruments (heliometer, telescopes, microscopes) and long-term, patient measurement to ensure precision; these laborious methods prepare the way for higher views of laws of the universe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep imagination separate from observational labor
rubrics_metrics.description: The observer's imagination should not dominate the laborious measurement process; the astronomer or botanist 'does not feel his imagination more excited' during precise work, and this preserves precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor sober, exact observation over imaginative embellishment during data collection—imaginative excitement is for later synthesis, not for the guarantee of precise labors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesize observations to discover general laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The discovery of each separate law of nature leads to the establishment of some other more general law or indicates its existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine multiplicity of observations by reasoning to trace mutual relations; generalization is the objective of experimental sciences—discover laws and trace their progressive generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish the roles of specialist collectors and synthesizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between those who collect and study individual details (specialists) and those who reveal relations and general results (synthesizers or authors of general works).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and respect both roles: specialists must be acquainted with phenomena particulars; synthesizers should reveal relations and present general outcomes accessible to broader audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make popular exposition accessible without losing profundity
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific works intended for general readers should be made manifest without necessarily appealing to fundamental technical principles; the picture of nature can be drawn intelligibly despite some lack of technical distinctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for conciseness that is 'devoid of superficiality' — present general truths clearly, remove technical scaffolding when possible, but avoid oversimplification that sacrifices depth (Laplace praised as presenting results free from processes of demonstration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dignified, grave, and animated language for science
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific subjects may be treated in language at once dignified, grave, and animated, enabling those outside specialized life to access scientific ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid flippant or patronizing tones in popular science; employ elevated but lively prose to open science as a source of intellectual enjoyment for wider classes of society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base physical history on empiricism, not on speculative abstraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical history of the universe must be based upon facts registered by science and tested by the intellect, and should not rise to the 'perilous abstractions of a purely rational science of nature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the work to rational empiricism—describe and generalize from observed phenomena rather than advancing purely speculative metaphysics; acknowledge when topics exceed physical explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary mutual enrichment and application
rubrics_metrics.description: As the special sciences advance, they mutually enrich each other and yield laws of more general application (e.g., voltaic pile revealed links among electric, magnetic, and chemical phenomena).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage discoveries across disciplines to create concise, connected generalizations; expect advances in one area (meteorology, optics, electromagnetism) to illuminate others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal appreciation of all branches; avoid dismissing 'pure theory'
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not stigmatize branches of knowledge as 'purely theoretical'—isolated observations may conceal the germ of major discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat mathematical, experimental, and descriptive branches with equal respect; recognize that apparently theoretical findings (e.g., polarization of light) can have far-reaching practical and explanatory consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove methodological scaffolding when presenting results
rubrics_metrics.description: An edifice cannot produce a striking effect until the scaffolding used during its erection is removed; the public exposition should not burden readers with all methods of demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing for a general audience, omit excessive methodological minutiae that obscure the main ideas, while ensuring the presentation retains intellectual rigor and truthfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid superficial half-knowledge and dogmatic pretensions in public discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Superficial half-knowledge, introduced into general conversation, yields alarmist phantoms (e.g., exaggerated fears about comet collisions or climate deterioration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about propagating poorly understood scientific claims; combat dogmatic pretensions by emphasizing sound empirical reasoning and long-term measurement records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits and scope of physical explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Physics aims to discover laws of material phenomena; 'all that exceeds this goes beyond the province of the physical description of the universe' and belongs to higher speculative views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly delimit what physical science can explain and when a question moves into metaphysics or speculative philosophy (citing Kant's limits of physical explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Travelers and observers must be scientifically informed and guided by reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Narratives of distant travels are instructive only when the traveler is acquainted with the condition of the science he would enlarge and is guided by reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field observers and travelers should collect data with knowledge of current scientific frameworks so their observations can be integrated into broader scientific understanding; unguided narratives are of limited instructional value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be alert to new phenomena revealed by improved instruments and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvements in instruments (microscopes, telescopes) and methods reveal unknown regions and intermediate links (e.g., microscopic infusoria, connecting organic forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continually employ and refine instruments and long-term observation to discover transition forms and relations; expect previously isolated phenomena to be connected by better tools and wider comparative study.
